question: What claim about the yoginī named Icchā requires her to extend to the end of Māyā by the supreme will and through the siddhas?
premises: The yoginī named Icchā is in view.
She extends to the end of Māyā.
This occurs by the supreme will and by the siddhas.
inference: The yoginī Icchā, by supreme will and through the siddhas, extends to the end of Māyā.
uncertainties: The precise agency of the siddhas in this extension is not specified by this verse alone.
plain_english: The yoginī named Icchā, by supreme will, extends to the end of Māyā through the siddhas.
